_comment: Curated divergence ages (Ma) for key nodes, keyed by OTT id. Each entry is one published estimate with its citation; 'note' says which node the source actually dates (crown or stem/total group), which may differ from the OTT clade it is attached to. kind: 'clock' = molecular-clock estimate (ma = reported point estimate; min_ma/max_ma = the reported credibility interval); 'fossil_minimum' = age of the oldest accepted fossil, a minimum for the lineage it belongs to, not the divergence itself (ma = reported age; min_ma/max_ma = the dating uncertainty of the fossil horizon, or the age bracket when no point age is given); 'biomarker' = molecular-fossil evidence. No TimeTree values are used anywhere. check: 'full_text' = the value, interval, units, node and citation were checked against the full text of the cited work (publisher version, or the authors' accepted/submitted manuscript where that is the open copy; the note says which); 'abstract' = only the abstract (and any open supplement named in the note) could be read, so the node definition and interval have not been confirmed from the full text.

304358.note: Re-Os first appearance of Bangiomorpha pubescens, 1.047 +0.013/-0.017 Ga. A crown-group red alga, so a minimum for crown Eukaryota (and for the red-green algal split). Checked against the abstract and the open GSA Data Repository supplement (2018030); the article itself is not open access.

Crown-group sterane biomarkers ('crown-steroids') first appear ~800 Ma (Tonian). Older protosteroids (a 'Protosterol Biota', from at least 1,640 Ma to ~800 Ma) are attributed to protosterol-producing bacteria and/or stem-group eukaryotes. Read in the authors' manuscript (HAL hal-04273175).

691846.note: Crown Metazoa, 833-650 Ma, after integrating all sources of uncertainty explored (data partitioning, calibration strategy, clock model); the authors stress that current data cannot narrow this much.

117569.note: Ikaria wariootia, Ediacara Member, South Australia; body 1.9-6.7 mm long (maximum ~7 mm). Interpreted as a total-group bilaterian (the probable maker of Helminthoidichnites traces), so a minimum for the bilaterian stem (split from Cnidaria), not for crown Bilateria. No radiometric date: 560-551 Ma is by correlation with the White Sea assemblage.

611099.note: Saccorhytus coronarius, Kuanchuanpu Formation (Fortunian, 531.8-536.4 Ma), South China. Resolved as a total-group ecdysozoan (basal ecdysozoan, panarthropod or cycloneuralian), not a deuterostome; a minimum for the ecdysozoan stem, not for crown Ecdysozoa. Read in the authors' accepted manuscript (University of Bristol repository).

632179.note: Oldest trilobite body fossils, ca. 521 Ma (base of Cambrian Series 2). Trilobites are crown-group euarthropods, so this is a minimum for crown Euarthropoda. Trilobite-like trace fossils (Rusophycus) are older (early Fortunian).

1062253.note: The abstract's 'origin of insects', Early Ordovician (~479 Ma). The full text was not accessible, so whether this dates crown Insecta, crown Hexapoda or a stem node, and its credibility interval, have not been confirmed.

1048707.note: The abstract's 'origin of insect flight', Early Devonian (~406 Ma). The full text was not accessible, so whether this is the crown-Pterygota node, and its credibility interval, have not been confirmed.

150772.note: Mites are among the earliest occurrences in the Rhynie and Windyfield cherts (Early Devonian). Age 407.6 +/- 2.2 Ma (40Ar/39Ar), the age the authors favour. The paper does not place the mites within Acari; Acari is not monophyletic in the Open Tree synthesis.

391142.note: Crown Volvocaceae (node C in Fig. 2), 200 Ma (95% credibility interval 179-222), by which the spheroidal body plan had evolved. The volvocine lineage diverged from unicellular relatives ~234 Ma (209-260) and was multicellular by ~223 Ma (200-248).

56610.note: Crown Embryophyta (land plants), 95% HPD across all topologies 515.1-470.0 Ma (middle Cambrian to Early Ordovician). Across alternative dating strategies it ranges from 583.1 to 470.0 Ma.
